hints.content:
Let's separate the variables.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=f(x)g(y)
\\\\
\dfrac{1}{g(y)}\,dy&=f(x)\,dx
\\\\
\dfrac{1}{e^{-y}}\,dy&=3x^{-2}\,dx
\\\\
\displaystyle \int e^y\,dy&=\displaystyle \int 3x^{-2}\,dx
\end{align}$

Kofi separated the variables correctly.

Let's integrate.

$\begin{align}
\displaystyle\int e^y\,dy&=\displaystyle\int 3x^{-2}\,dx
\\\\
e^y&=-\dfrac{3}{x}+C
\end{align}$

Kofi forgot to add $C$ immediately to represent the information lost between a function and its derivative. It is not equivalent to wait until the end of isolating $y$ and then to add $C$.
In conclusion, step 2 is incorrect. The right-hand side of the equation should be $-\dfrac{3}{x}+C$.

question.content:
Kofi tried to solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^{-2}e^{-y}$. This is his work:

$\begin{align}
&&\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=3x^{-2}e^{-y}
\\\\
\text{Step 1:}&&\displaystyle\int e^y\,dy&=\displaystyle\int 3x^{-2}\,dx
\\\\
\text{Step 2:}&&e^y&=-\dfrac{3}{x}
\\\\
\text{Step 3:}&&\ln(e^y)&=\ln\left(-\dfrac{3}{x}\right)
\\\\
\text{Step 4:}&&y&=\ln\left(-\dfrac{3}{x}\right)+C
\end{align}$

**Is Kofi's work correct? If not, what is his mistake?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: When Kofi integrates, he needs to add a constant to the right side of the equation immediately.  It is not equivalent to wait until the end of the algebraic manipulations, then add the constant.

choices.content: **Step 1** is incorrect. The separation of variables wasn't done correctly.

choices.clue: When Kofi integrates, he needs to add a constant to the right side of the equation immediately.  It is not equivalent to wait until the end of the algebraic manipulations, then add the constant.
choices.content: **Step 2** is incorrect. The right-hand side of the equation should be $-\dfrac{3}{x}+C$.

choices.clue: While the domain of the natural logarithm function only includes positive numbers, the expression $-\dfrac{3}{x}$ could be positive.
choices.content: **Step 3** is incorrect. Kofi should not have a negative symbol inside of a natural logarithm.
